battle.name: 委內瑞拉獨立戰爭
battle.theater: 委內瑞拉中部卡拉布索戰場
battle.brief: 1811年4月19日代表大會在卡拉卡斯宣告獨立，委內瑞拉獨立戰爭自此爆發。戰爭經一度淪陷、玻利瓦爾率軍翻越安第斯山北進，終於1821年6月24日的卡拉布索戰役定勝。卡面輪發手槍是十六世紀西班牙的後膛手槍，1811年已讓位給燧發手槍，只在軍官隨身自衛的傳統上留有餘痕。

kit.name: 輪發手槍
kit.history: 最早的後膛手槍。機械太貴，只給火槍隊的軍官與近衛。

countries: 交戰一方是西班牙王國在委內瑞拉的殖民統治當局與西班牙皇家陸軍。卡那利亞斯王國在委內瑞拉都督轄區派駐常備營、騎兵營與炮兵隊，徵用克里奧爾人與土著民兵充當後勤與步哨，並以王室軍官、總督府與都督府構成指揮系統；地方實權長期在效忠派手中，1813至1814年皇家軍一度奪回北部各省，1815年更由巴勃羅·莫里略率領遠征軍自西班牙本土抵達恢復殖民統治，1816年後改以米格爾·德·拉·托雷主持反擊游擊，末段殘軍由曼努埃爾·瑪麗亞·托雷斯等率領，另有拉薩羅首領何塞·托馬斯·波維斯率領的效忠派民兵充當耳目與打手，海上則有西班牙海軍封鎖委內瑞拉沿岸港口與河流出口。另一方是委內瑞拉愛國派：由卡拉斯卡、瓦倫西亞等各省代表組成的代表大會於1811年成立並主持國政，先後建立三屆共和國，流亡海外的西蒙·玻利瓦爾於1816年率數百名流亡者在奧庫馬雷登陸，訓練並壯大軍隊，1817年奪取馬拉開波省，1819年越過安第斯山解放紐格蘭達，1821年在卡拉布索擊敗皇家軍主力；其下屬有拉薩羅出身的愛國派騎兵與卡薩納雷槍騎兵，以及民兵、遊擊隊與地方議會提供的後勤支援。戰爭後期雙方一度捲入代表大會內部中央集權派與聯邦派之間的內戰，波哥大方面的桑坦德與玻利瓦爾在1821年8月的庫庫塔交鋒即其一端。
countriesEn: On one side stood the Spanish colonial administration in Venezuela together with the Royal Army of Spain. The Crown kept permanent infantry, cavalry and artillery battalions in the Captaincy General of Venezuela, drew Criollo and indigenous militia into supply work and outpost duty, and ran a chain of command through royal officers, the viceregal government and the captaincy general. Local power stayed largely in loyalist hands: royalist troops retook the northern provinces in 1813 and 1814, and in 1815 Pablo Morillo arrived from Spain with an expeditionary force to restore colonial rule. From 1816 the counter-insurgency was directed by Miguel de la Torre, while the last loyalist brigades were led by officers such as Manuel María Torres, and the llanero caudillo José Tomás Boves led loyalist militia that served the Crown as eyes and fists in the plains; the Spanish navy blockaded the Venezuelan coast and the river mouths. On the other side stood the Venezuelan patriot cause. A congress of delegates from Caracas, Valencia and the other provinces was formed in 1811 and governed the country, passing through three successive republics, while Simón Bolívar, returning from exile, landed at Ocumare in 1816 with several hundred men, trained and expanded an army, seized the province of Maracaibo in 1817, crossed the Andes to liberate New Granada in 1819, and destroyed the main royalist field army at Carabobo in 1821. Under him served patriot cavalry drawn from the llaneros, the Casanare lancers, together with militias, guerrilla bands and the local councils that supplied the army. In its later phase the struggle also swallowed the civil war inside the congress between the centralists and the federalists, of which the encounter at Cúcuta near Bogotá in August 1821 was one expression.
people: 西蒙·玻利瓦爾是這場戰爭的主導者。他是委內瑞拉土生克里奧爾人，1810年參與接管卡拉斯卡的愛國委員會，1811年當選代表大會議員並主持《獨立法典》的起草，1813年出任短命的第三共和國武裝總司令，1814年在瓦倫西亞兵敗後流亡英屬圭亞那，並赴倫敦遊說英國支持美洲獨立。1816年他自奧庫馬雷登陸，1817年發動馬拉開波征討戰役，1819年率約二千六百人翻越安第斯山、解放波哥大，1821年6月24日在卡拉布索擊敗皇家軍，1822年解放基多，1823年回國主持清剿西班牙殘部，最終於1830年12月病逝於馬拉凱附近的莊園。弗朗西斯科·德·米蘭達是獨立運動最早的推動者，他以將軍與議員身分在1811年代表大會上主持獨立議案，1812年因英國護航船被扣而被迫放棄波多卡貝略，1813年再赴歐洲尋求外援，1816年在加勒比海岸的囚禁中病逝。何塞·安東尼奧·派斯是拉薩羅出身的騎兵首領，在卡拉布索以騎兵扭轉戰局，1821年後成為執政者，1823年率軍掃蕩東部的殘餘西班牙縱隊。皇家軍方面，米格爾·德·拉·托雷主持1816年之後的殲滅戰並在卡拉布索擔任統帥，托馬斯·莫拉萊斯率軍攻破瓦倫西亞，巴勃羅·莫里略率遠征軍恢復殖民統治，何塞·托馬斯·波維斯率拉薩羅效忠派游擊隊在平原上作戰。何塞·安德烈斯·德·拉斯·赫拉斯上校指揮卡薩納雷槍騎兵，安東尼奧·何塞·蘇克雷以軍官身分在卡拉布索參戰，日後解放基多並在阿亞庫喬決定戰局。
peopleEn: Simón Bolívar was the leading figure of the war. A Venezuelan-born Criollo, he took part in the seizure of the Junta Patriótica in Caracas in 1810, was elected a deputy to the congress of 1811 and helped draft the Act of Independence, and became the armed chief of the short-lived Third Republic in 1813. After the defeat at Valencia in 1814 he was exiled in British Guiana and travelled to London to press British support for American independence. He landed at Ocumare in 1816, opened the Maracaibo campaign in 1817, led some twenty-six hundred men across the Andes in 1819 and liberated Bogotá, beat the royalists at Carabobo on 24 June 1821, freed Quito in 1822, and came back in 1823 to direct the mopping-up of the remaining Spanish forces; he died of illness at a plantation near Maracay in December 1830. Francisco de Miranda was the earliest promoter of the movement: as general and deputy he carried the independence motion in the congress of 1811, was forced to abandon Puerto Cabello in 1812 when a British escorting ship was detained, returned to Europe in 1813 seeking foreign aid, and died in captivity on the Caribbean coast in 1816. José Antonio Páez, a llanero-born cavalry chief, turned the battle at Carabobo with his horsemen, became the ruler of the country after 1821 and led the 1823 campaigns that swept the eastern remnants of the Spanish brigades. On the Spanish side Miguel de la Torre directed the war of extermination from 1816 and commanded at Carabobo, Tomás Morales stormed Valencia, Pablo Morillo brought the expeditionary army that restored colonial rule, and José Tomás Boves led the loyalist llanero bands in the plains. Colonel José Andrés de Las Heras commanded the Casanare lancers, and Antonio José de Sucre fought at Carabobo as an officer, later freeing Quito and deciding the battle of Ayacucho.
kits: 卡面這件輪發手槍是十六世紀初的德製輪式發條後膛手槍傳入西班牙後的產物，金屬機匣內藏發條與棘輪，扣下扳機時發條帶動擊錘撞擊燧石，點燃後膛的火藥，再由擊錘撞擊底火完成射擊，槍管後膛以螺紋閉合，可反覆裝填。由於機構造價高昂，一把只配給火槍隊的軍官與近衛使用，用途多為近身自衛、值夜與儀仗，而不是列陣齊射的主力兵器；到1811年，軍中早已改用燧發手槍，輪發手槍淪為少數資深軍官手中與軍械庫裡的舊物。戰役中真正吃重的是西班牙皇家陸軍的燧發滑膛槍，槍身約一百四十公分，配刺刀，並以六磅與十二磅野戰炮及少量臼炮支援，部分部隊以定量紙包包裝火藥與球彈分發；軍官佩帶七吋至九吋的燧發手槍，騎兵使用龍騎兵槍、佩劍與彎刀。愛國派民兵以獵槍、長矛、砍刀與農具改製的武器作戰，拉薩羅騎兵主要靠長矛、馬刀與散彈槍，套索與套索槍則用於平原上絆纏對手，缺彈時甚至以標槍與石塊擲擊。運兵方面，奧里諾科河與馬拉開波湖靠平底貨船與大駁船載運士兵、糧食與軍火，另有縱帆雙桅船與近海帆船在海岸線上活動，關鍵的兵工原料硝石主要來自奧里諾科上游圭亞納一帶的鹽石硝礦，1816年玻利瓦爾的奧里諾科遠征即以控制這些礦場為目標。
kitsEn: The wheel-lock pistol on the card face is the sixteenth-century descendant of the German wheel-lock mechanism that reached Spain. Its metal lock holds a mainspring and a ratchet: pulling the trigger lets the spring drive the hammer onto the frizzen, which throws sparks into the priming pan of the breech, and the hammer then strikes the pan to fire. The threaded breech is closed by a plug, so the pistol can be loaded repeatedly. Because the mechanism was so expensive, a wheel-lock was issued only to the officers and guards of the musket units, and its employment was close protection, night watch and pageantry rather than the massed volley fire of the line; by 1811 the flintlock pistol had long displaced it, and the wheel-lock survived as a veteran officer's personal weapon and as obsolete stock in the arsenals. The real weight of the campaign fell on the Spanish flintlock smoothbore musket, about 140 centimetres long, with bayonet, supported by 6- and 12-pounder field guns and a few mortars, and some units received measured paper cartridges of powder and ball. Officers carried flintlock pistols of seven to nine inches, and cavalry used carbines, straight swords and sabres. Patriot militia fought with hunting guns, pikes, machetes and farm tools turned into weapons; llanero horsemen relied on the lance, the sabre and the shotgun, with the lasso and lasso-gun used to trip opponents on the plains, and when ammunition ran short they even hurled javelins and stones. Troops, food and munitions were moved on the Orinoco and Lake Maracaibo in flat-bottomed boats and lighters, with schooners and coastal craft working the shoreline. The critical raw material, saltpetre, came from the nitrate deposits of the Guayana highlands on the upper Orinoco, and seizing those mines was one of the aims of Bolívar's Orinoco expedition of 1816.
tactics: 開戰方式是城市自衛與奪取武器庫。1811年4月19日代表大會在卡拉斯卡的聖塔奧拉城堡宣布獨立，市區民兵接管武器與港口，皇家當局退往內陸據點。愛國派以民兵為骨幹，訓練與彈藥不足，多倚賴市區的群眾動員；皇家軍則利用正規營的射擊與炮兵優勢，配合拉薩羅效忠派在平原上的機動作戰，破壞道路、襲擊城鎮與游擊隊的基地，企圖以斷糧與游擊削弱愛國派。1813與1814年的瓦倫西亞攻防最能說明雙方差距：第一次圍城失敗，第二次圍城自1813年3月延續到1814年5月，玻利瓦爾在野外的拉普埃爾塔德洛斯法爾塞斯戰役失利後被迫撤退，瓦倫西亞終被托馬斯·莫拉萊斯攻破，愛國派重整旗鼓再入山區，以小股遊擊隊切斷皇家軍的通信與糧道。1816年8月6日玻利瓦爾在奧庫馬雷登陸並發表宣言，12月3日夜襲安戈斯圖拉的皇家軍營地卻因協同與警戒不周而慘敗，損失慘重，迫使他轉入奧里諾科河三角洲，以控制鹽石硝礦與擴軍再圖。1817年馬拉開波征討戰役是愛國派最成功的一次進攻：玻利瓦爾率部越過帕丘里托山進入馬拉開波省，攻取馬拉開波城，7月26日在湖上以陸戰隊攻擊皇家艦隊奪取湖面控制權，再沿內格羅河分兵襲擊卡布魯斯。與此同時，1817年12月23日的巴爾加斯沼澤之戰因地形泥濘、騎兵驚潰而失敗，新格拉納達的進攻被推遲。1819年5月玻利瓦爾自安戈斯圖拉率軍出發，經帕拉莫與塔馬拉梅山道翻越安第斯山，行程約十日，糧秣短缺、人馬大量脫落，12月7日在巴約卡山口擊敗皇家軍並進占波哥大。1820年西班牙自由革命削弱了馬德里的支援，1821年1月7日的科西亞塔迫使皇家軍退出卡拉卡斯。6月24日的卡拉布索戰役，玻利瓦爾把主力佈置在山麓斜坡，令三個縱隊在皇家軍正面展開時分別壓向右翼，皇家軍的槍騎兵因不願在陡坡火網下強攻而停滯，僵局中玻利瓦爾集中縱隊強攻中央陣線，皇家軍騎兵陣形崩潰，敗兵在沼澤地帶互相擠壓而潰散，天黑前戰鬥結束。戰後數年，愛國派以縱隊掃蕩方式消滅北部與東部的殘餘西班牙守軍，直至1823年對方放棄委內瑞拉本土。內戰一線則以1821年8月25日波哥大近郊的庫庫塔戰役為代表，玻利瓦爾擊敗聯邦派首領桑坦德，暴露了共和國內部的裂痕。
tacticsEn: The war opened with urban self-defence and the seizure of the arsenals. On 19 April 1811 the congress proclaimed independence at the Castillo de Santa Rosa in Caracas, the city militia took over the weapons and the port, and the royal authorities withdrew to inland posts. The patriots rested on militia, short of training and ammunition and dependent on mass mobilisation in the towns; the royalists played on the fire and artillery of their regular battalions, combined with the mobility of the loyalist llaneros on the plains, cutting roads, raiding towns and guerrilla bases in an attempt to strangle the patriot cause by hunger and harassment. The fighting over Valencia in 1813 and 1814 shows the gap between the two sides best. The first siege failed, and the second ran from March 1813 to May 1814; after Bolívar lost the field engagement at La Puerta de los Falces he was forced to withdraw, Valencia was stormed by Tomás Morales, and the patriot cause regrouped in the mountains where small guerrilla bands cut the royalist communications and supply lines. On 6 August 1816 Bolívar landed at Ocumare and issued his declaration, but the night attack on the royalist camp at Angostura on 3 December went badly wrong because of poor coordination and inadequate pickets, and the severe losses pushed him into the Orinoco delta, where he took the saltpetre mines and rebuilt his army. The Maracaibo campaign of 1817 was the most successful patriot offensive: Bolívar crossed the Pachurito range into the province of Maracaibo, took the city of Maracaibo, and on 26 July struck the royalist squadron on the lake with his infantry to seize command of the water, then split his force along the Rio Negro to raid Cabrús. Meanwhile the battle of the Pantano de Vargas on 23 December 1817 was lost because the boggy ground panicked the cavalry, and the New Granada campaign was postponed. In May 1819 Bolívar set out from Angostura, crossed the Andes by the páramo route and the Tamalame track in about ten days with short rations and heavy loss of men and animals, and on 7 December broke the royalist army at the Boyacá pass and entered Bogotá. The liberal revolution in Spain in 1820 weakened Madrid's support, and the Cosiata of 7 January 1821 drove the royalists out of Caracas. At Carabobo on 24 June the patriots were posted on the lower slopes; as the royalist line deployed frontally, three patriot columns pressed against its flanks, and the royalist lancers stalled rather than charge up the steep slope under the muskets' fire. From that stalemate Bolívar concentrated his columns against the centre, the royalist cavalry formation broke, and the routed troops jammed each other in the marshes before the fighting ended at nightfall. In the years after Carabobo patriot columns swept the north and east, destroying the remaining Spanish garrisons until in 1823 the Crown gave up Venezuelan soil. The civil-war line is represented by the battle of Cúcuta near Bogotá on 25 August 1821, in which Bolívar defeated the federalist leader Santander and laid bare the cracks inside the republic.
data: 這場戰爭自1811年4月19日至1823年，前後約十二年，主要戰役集中在1813至1814、1816至1817、1819與1821四個階段。1811年的委內瑞拉總人口估計不足一百萬，任何一支軍隊都只能從極小的兵源中抽成，玻利瓦爾1816年在奧庫馬雷登陸時只帶數百名流亡者，1817年馬拉開波征討戰役投入的兵力約一千餘人，1819年越嶺的遠征軍常被記為約二千六百人，馬匹數千，隨身只帶數週口糧，越嶺歷時約十日，途中人馬大量耗損。1816年12月3日安戈斯圖拉之役，愛國派夜襲損失約六百人，皇家軍損失不足百人；1817年12月23日巴爾加斯沼澤之役慘敗後，新格拉納達的戰事整整推遲兩年，直到1819年12月7日巴約卡之役才拿下波哥大，該役皇家軍損失約一千七百人，並被繳獲火槍數百支與全部軍餉。卡拉布索戰役是全役的決戰：1821年6月24日的愛國軍常被記為約六千人，皇家軍常被記為約九千人，雙方火炮合計數十門，史料對這兩個數字說法不一，只能作概數看待；戰後愛國軍傷亡約一千五百人，皇家軍陣亡、受傷與被俘合計約兩千人，另有數百名傷者因沼澤地形無法救運。第二回合倫西亞之圍自1813年3月至1814年5月，歷時逾一年，圍城方最終未能守住城市。縱觀全役，西班牙方面的常備軍規模始終有限，多在數千之數，而愛國派靠分裂的民兵與拉薩羅騎兵在多條戰線上牽制對方，戰爭的物資基礎幾乎全靠河海運輸與進口火藥維持。
dataEn: The war ran from 19 April 1811 to 1823, roughly twelve years, with the main campaigns concentrated in four phases: 1813 to 1814, 1816 to 1817, 1819 and 1821. The total population of Venezuela in 1811 is estimated at under a million, so any army could be raised only from an extremely small pool of men: Bolívar landed at Ocumare in 1816 with only several hundred exiles, the Maracaibo campaign of 1817 committed about a thousand men, and the expedition that crossed the Andes in 1819 is commonly put at some twenty-six hundred men with thousands of horses and only a few weeks of rations, taking about ten days over the crossing with heavy losses of men and animals. In the action at Angostura on 3 December 1816 the patriot night attack cost about six hundred men against fewer than a hundred royalist casualties; after the defeat in the Pantano de Vargas on 23 December 1817 the New Granada war was put off for two full years, and Bogotá only fell with the victory at Boyacá on 7 December 1819, in which the royalists lost about seventeen hundred men and surrendered several hundred muskets and the whole war chest. Carabobo was the decisive battle of the war: on 24 June 1821 the patriot army is usually given as about six thousand men against about nine thousand royalists, with some dozens of guns between them, and the sources disagree on those two figures, so they can only be treated as approximations. Patriot casualties came to roughly fifteen hundred, and royalist dead, wounded and captured together to about two thousand, with several hundred more wounded unable to be evacuated because of the marshes. The second siege of Valencia lasted from March 1813 to May 1814, more than a year, and ended with the besiegers losing the city. Across the whole war the royalist regular army remained limited in size, generally in the low thousands, while the patriots countered with fragmented militia and llanero cavalry operating on several fronts at once; the material basis of the struggle was maintained almost entirely by river and coastal transport and by imported powder.
cause: 直接起因是1808年西班牙王位危機帶來的權力真空。1808年拿破崙廢黜波旁王室、囚禁斐迪南七世，消息傳到委內瑞拉後，首都卡拉斯卡的市議會要求建立自治並效忠新君，卻得不到母國的回應，第一屆省議會在阿拉瓜達提出的自治方案也被駁回，克里奧爾精英於是轉向分離。委內瑞拉在西班牙帝國的經濟地位不低，可可、咖啡、棉花與蔗糖大量輸出，卻長期受母國對殖民地貿易與稅收的嚴格限制，本地出身的克里奧爾人自認有權參政，卻被在地的半島西班牙人擠出官職，這種政治與經濟上的雙重排擠累積成分離訴求。外部刺激同樣強烈：美國獨立與法國革命提供了可援引的先例，拿破崙戰爭牽制了西班牙的兵力，南美各地自1810年起相繼起義，更給委內瑞拉示範。1810年4月卡拉斯卡成立愛國委員會接管市政，1811年4月19日代表大會宣告獨立，7月5日簽署《委內瑞拉獨立法典》並成立第一共和國，戰爭由是全面展開。值得注意的是，衝突一開始並非西班牙王國投入全部國力的一場決戰，而是地方軍與民兵之間的反覆較量，這也解釋了為何戰事能拖成十二年。
causeEn: The immediate cause was the power vacuum created by the Spanish succession crisis of 1808. After Napoleon deposed the Bourbon king and imprisoned Ferdinand VII, news reached Venezuela and the municipal council of Caracas demanded local autonomy and loyalty to the new sovereign, but the mother country gave no answer; the autonomy proposals of the first provincial deputation at Alaguitas were rejected as well, and the Criollo elite turned to separation. Venezuela's standing in the Spanish empire was not low: cocoa, coffee, cotton and sugar were exported in quantity, yet the colonies were kept under strict metropolitan control of trade and taxation, and locally born Criollos who considered themselves entitled to a share in government were pushed out of office by the peninsulares. That double exclusion, political and economic, accumulated into a case for secession. Outside stimulus was just as strong. American independence and the French Revolution supplied usable precedents, the Napoleonic wars tied down Spain's armies, and the rising in South America from 1810 onward gave Venezuela its example. In April 1810 Caracas formed the Junta Patriótica and took over the municipality; on 19 April 1811 the congress proclaimed independence; on 5 July it signed the Act of Independence of Venezuela and founded the First Republic, and the war opened in full. It should be noted that the conflict did not begin as a set-piece battle in which the whole power of Spain was committed, but as a repeated contest between provincial forces and militias, which is part of the reason it dragged on for twelve years.
impact: 獨立之後，委內瑞拉並沒有立刻獲得安寧，反而走入更長的內戰。1811年7月的《獨立法典》與1813年瓦倫西亞制憲會議制定的憲法，是南美洲最早的成文憲制文本之一，也把地方議會代表制、主權在民與公民權等觀念帶入政治。1821年玻利瓦爾召集安戈斯圖拉制憲會議，成立以委內瑞拉、紐格蘭達與厄瓜多爾為成員的大哥倫比亞聯邦，1822年攻下基多，1823年平定西班牙殘部，戰線又延伸進秘魯，1824年的胡寧與阿亞庫喬之役最終把西班牙在南美洲的統治送進墳墓。就軍史而言，這場戰爭確立了幾種做法：以民轉軍快速擴編、以拉薩羅騎兵與卡薩納雷槍騎兵補足西班牙步兵與炮兵的優勢、以河海運輸解決內陸補給、以游擊破壞拖延敵軍；這些做法隨著玻利瓦爾的軍隊後來走遍南美，被其他獨立軍隊仿效。政治上，這場戰爭把拉薩羅出身的軍人推上前台，形成委內瑞拉以軍事實力主導政治的傳統，1820年代至1830年代中央集權派與聯邦派在各省連年交火，1830年玻利瓦爾病逝、胡安·比戈·加斯通執政後聯邦派起兵，聯邦主義與中央集權之爭成為此後一世紀委內瑞拉政治的主線，1859至1863年的聯邦戰爭之後以聯邦公約收場，中央集權與地方自治的取捨仍擺在每一代政治人面前。戰爭造成的破壞、徵發與清算，使北部各省的農業與城鎮在1813至1814年的反攻中受創最重，此後委內瑞拉在國際上長期孤立，直到二十世紀初的借款糾紛與封鎖危機。
impactEn: Independence did not bring Venezuela an immediate peace; it led into a longer civil war. The Act of Independence of July 1811 and the constitution drawn up by the constituent assembly at Valencia in 1813 were among the earliest written constitutional texts in South America, and they carried the ideas of provincial representation, popular sovereignty and citizenship into Venezuelan politics. In 1821 Bolívar convened the congress at Angostura and founded the Gran Colombia federation of Venezuela, New Granada and Ecuador; he took Quito in 1822, pacified the last Spanish forces in 1823, and the war front extended into Peru, where Huamanga and Ayacucho in 1824 finally sealed the fate of Spanish rule in South America. In military terms the war established a number of practices: fast expansion through militia conversion, the use of llanero horsemen and Casanare lancers to offset the Spanish advantage in infantry and artillery, the movement of men and supplies by river and coastal shipping, and the harassment of the enemy by guerrilla destruction. These practices travelled with Bolívar's army across South America and were copied by other independence armies. Politically the war pushed soldier-statesmen of llanero origin to the front and established the tradition of military power dominating Venezuelan politics. Through the 1820s and 1830s centralists and federalists fought province by province; after Bolívar died in 1830 and Juan Vicente Gómez took over, the federalists rose again, and the contest between federalism and centralism became the main line of Venezuelan politics for the following century, ending only with the Federal Pact after the Federal War of 1859 to 1863, with the choice between strong central government and provincial autonomy still placed before every generation of politicians. The destruction, requisitions and reprisals of the war hit the agriculture and the towns of the northern provinces hardest during the royalist counter-offensive of 1813 and 1814, and Venezuela remained internationally isolated for a long time afterwards, until the loan disputes and blockade crisis of the early twentieth century.
result: 1821年6月24日的卡拉布索戰役是全役的樞紐。玻利瓦爾以縱隊強攻擊破米格爾·德·拉·托雷的陣線，皇家軍騎兵崩潰，傷者與被擠壓的散兵在卡拉布索沼澤中大量失去戰鬥力，主力被逐回內陸。玻利瓦爾隨即在北方向清剿殘敵，1821年11月召開安戈斯圖拉制憲會議，同年12月進軍波哥大，並在1821年8月25日的庫庫塔戰役中擊敗聯邦派首領桑坦德，確立中央集權一派在聯邦內的優勢，1822年1月24日的皮欽查之役解放基多，委內瑞拉方面的戰事自此與大哥倫比亞全局連成一體。最後一段收尾由何塞·安東尼奧·派斯等人完成：1823年，愛國派縱隊在委內瑞拉北部與東部相繼消滅西班牙的殘餘旅團，殘兵退入據點與海上，部分西班牙守軍延至1825年才最終撤離，委內瑞拉的獨立至此成為既成事實；1826年大哥倫比亞解體後，委內瑞拉以聯邦共和國的形式繼續存在，並承認玻利瓦爾為第一任總統。勝利的代價同樣沉重：戰爭留下的軍人政治傳統與省際對立，使新生的共和國在創建後十年間就捲入連年內戰，1830年玻利瓦爾病逝，1831年聯邦派起兵，這條裂痕一直延伸到十九世紀末與二十世紀，成為委內瑞拉現代政治最深的伏筆。
resultEn: The battle of Carabobo on 24 June 1821 was the hinge of the whole war. Bolívar broke Miguel de la Torre's line with a concentrated column assault; the royalist cavalry formation collapsed, and the wounded and the jostled fugitives lost their fighting power in large numbers in the marshes of Carabobo while the main body was driven back inland. Bolívar then swept the north in pursuit, convened the congress at Angostura in November 1821, and marched into Bogotá in December, while his victory over the federalist leader Santander at Cúcuta on 25 August 1821 gave the centralist party the upper hand inside the federation. The freeing of Quito at Pichincha on 24 January 1822 tied the Venezuelan front into the wider strategy of Gran Colombia. The last stage was closed by José Antonio Páez and his companions: in 1823 patriot columns destroyed the remaining Spanish brigades one after another in the north and east of Venezuela, the remnants falling back into their strongholds and onto the sea, and some Spanish garrisons did not leave until 1825. Venezuelan independence was by then a fait accompli, and after Gran Colombia broke up in 1826 the country continued as a federal republic with Bolívar as its first president. The cost of that victory was heavy. The military-political tradition and the provincial antagonisms left behind by the war threw the new republic into repeated civil war within a decade of its founding; Bolívar died in 1830, the federalists rose in 1831, and that fissure ran on into the late nineteenth and twentieth centuries as the deepest seed of modern Venezuelan politics.
